**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, RENEWAL).**

What I found:
- **Renewal mechanics — acceptable.** § 2 (p0011) is an evergreen term ("shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6"), and § 6(a) (p0032) gives either party a 15-day termination right when no SOW is outstanding. There is no auto-renewal, no non-renewal notice window, and no multi-year renewal term, so those limbs of the rule are met (exit is easier than our 30-day preferred position).
- **Price predictability — deviation.** § 3(b) (p0014) says "Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice to Company" — a unilateral, uncapped, unlimited-frequency uplift right. On an open-ended term this reproduces exactly the pricing risk the rule targets.

Redline (validated, ok:true): rates fixed for the duration of each Statement of Work; thereafter increases limited to once per 12 months, effective on 60 days' written notice, capped at the lesser of CPI-U and 3%, with a 5% cap flagged as the fallback.
